# 06 Steel-to-UCFT explicit strain-load interface and UHPC physical-anchor framework

Date: 2026-09-25

## A. Steel shell: explicit average axial shortening generated by the locked whole-face field

Let
alpha=pi/b, beta=pi/a_h,
g=sin(alpha x)sin(beta y),
phi=[1-cos(2N alpha x)][1-cos(2m beta y)],

Ws0=b q0 g+A0 phi,
Ws=b(q0+q)g+(A0+A)phi.

Define the compression-positive average geometric shortening

gbar_s =
(1/(2 b a_h)) int_0^b int_0^a_h [Ws,y^2-Ws0,y^2] dy dx.

All integrals can be performed analytically. The result is

gbar_s(q,A)=
pi^2 b^2/(8 a_h^2) (q^2+2q0 q)
+
64 b N^2 m^2/
[a_h^2(4N^2-1)(4m^2-1)]
(q0 A+q A0+q A)
+
3m^2 pi^2/(2a_h^2)(2A0 A+A^2).

This is GG + GL + LL in axial-shortening form.

At q=q0=0 and N=1 it reduces exactly to the previous Yun-Lu/Y-3 geometric shortening:
3m^2 pi^2/(2a_h^2)(2A0A+A^2).

## B. Elastic steel generalized strain-load law

The previously derived elastic whole-face force per unit transverse width is

p_s^E(q,A)=
[D_s B_bend - t_s P_mem]/[-J_x],

D_s=E_s t_s^3/[12(1-nu_s^2)],

with B_bend, P_mem and J_x already fully algebraic in file 03.

Therefore the whole-face end-shortening strain carried by the steel plate is

lambda_s^E(q,A)
=
p_s^E(q,A)/(E_s t_s)
+
gbar_s(q,A).

This is the explicit axial-strain/load interface required for UCFT.

For the one-global-mode UCFT reduction, the mean global curvature contribution at a steel face is

kappa_bar_y^g =
<pi^2 b q/a_h^2 sin(pi x/b) sin(pi y/a_h)>
=4 b q/a_h^2.

At signed steel-face offset z_s^+>0, z_s^-<0, the compression-positive kinematic end shortening is

Lambda_s^pm(lambda,q)
=
lambda - z_s^pm 4bq/a_h^2.

Hence the S1 compatibility equation is

lambda - z_s^pm 4bq/a_h^2
=
p_s^{E,pm}(q,A^pm)/(E_s t_s^pm)
+
gbar_s^pm(q,A^pm).

No steel area or thickness integration remains.

## C. Exact cubic condensation of A at fixed (lambda,q)

For fixed q write the elastic force as

p_s^E(q,A)=
[n0(q)+n1(q)A+n2(q)A^2+n3(q)A^3]/
[d0(q)+d1 A].

The denominator coefficients are

d0=(alpha/beta)[
64N^2m^2 b(q0+q)/((4N^2-1)(4m^2-1))
+3pi^2N^2 A0
],

d1=(alpha/beta)3pi^2N^2.

Let s=q0+q and define the already-derived algebraic harmonic contractions
K1=K_GG,GL,
K2=K_GL,GL,
K3=K_GL,LL,
K4=K_GG,LL,
K5=K_LL,LL.

Then the membrane polynomial before multiplication by E_s is

c0 =
b^3(q^2+2q0q)s K1
+b^2 s q A0 K2
+2b^2(q^2+2q0q)A0 K4
+2b q A0^2 K3,

c1 =
b^2 s^2 K2
+2b^2(q^2+2q0q)K4
+2bA0(2q0+3q)K3
+4A0^2K5,

c2 =
3b s K3+6A0K5,

c3=2K5.

With

B_q =
64 b q N^2m^2(alpha^2+beta^2)^2/
[(4N^2-1)(4m^2-1)alpha beta],

B_A =
pi^2[12N^4alpha^4+8N^2m^2alpha^2beta^2+12m^4beta^4]/
(alpha beta),

the numerator coefficients are

n0=D_s B_q+E_s t_s c0,
n1=D_s B_A+E_s t_s c1,
n2=E_s t_s c2,
n3=E_s t_s c3.

The geometric shortening is

gbar_s=g0+g1 A+g2 A^2,

g0 =
pi^2b^2/(8a_h^2)(q^2+2q0q)
+
64bN^2m^2/(a_h^2(4N^2-1)(4m^2-1)) q A0,

g1 =
64bN^2m^2/(a_h^2(4N^2-1)(4m^2-1))(q0+q)
+
3m^2pi^2 A0/a_h^2,

g2=3m^2pi^2/(2a_h^2).

Let
Lambda=lambda-z_s 4bq/a_h^2.

Multiplying the strain compatibility by d0+d1A gives the exact cubic

C3 A^3+C2 A^2+C1 A+C0=0,

C0=(Lambda-g0)d0-n0/(E_s t_s),

C1=(Lambda-g0)d1-g1d0-n1/(E_s t_s),

C2=-g1d1-g2d0-n2/(E_s t_s),

C3=-g2d1-n3/(E_s t_s).

Thus A^pm is not required to remain an iterative unknown in this reduced theory. At each (lambda,q), it can be obtained from the exact cubic formula, with the physical root selected by connected continuation from the previous state.

This is exact algebraic condensation inside the adopted finite Yun-Lu/Chen-Ji closure, not an empirical reduction.

## D. Steel contribution to the global q equation

The local phi-projection determines p_s^E. A separate global g-projection is still required for the composite UCFT q equilibrium. It must not be confused with setting A=0 in the local equation.

The membrane part can be generated from the same quadratic Airy potential. Define

K_GG,GG =
pi^2/128 (alpha^3/beta+beta^3/alpha).

Then the membrane generalized force conjugate to q is

P_mem,q =
-E_s[
2b^4(q^2+2q0q)(q0+q)K_GG,GG
+b^3(2(q0+q)L+(q^2+2q0q)(A0+A))K_GG,GL
+2b^2(q0+q)R K_GG,LL
+b^2L(A0+A)K_GL,GL
+bR(A0+A)K_GL,LL
],

where L=q0A+qA0+qA and R=2A0A+A^2.

The global bending projection is

B_q,g =
a_h b^3 q(alpha^2+beta^2)^2/4
+
64bA N^2m^2(alpha^2+beta^2)^2/
[(4N^2-1)(4m^2-1)alpha beta].

The homogeneous axial-force projection is

J_q,g =
-a_h b^3 alpha^2(q0+q)/4
-
64bN^2m^2 alpha(A0+A)/
[beta(4N^2-1)(4m^2-1)].

Therefore the steel-face contribution to the UCFT global q residual can be written explicitly as

R_q^s =
D_s B_q,g - t_s P_mem,q + p_s J_q,g.

For the composite plate the total global equation is

R_q^U + R_q^{s,+}+R_q^{s,-}=0

(with any separately retained web term added only if that theory version explicitly includes it).

After A^pm(lambda,q) is replaced by the cubic roots, this becomes one scalar global equation in q for each prescribed lambda.

The total axial load is then

P(lambda,q)=
N_U(lambda,q)
+b p_s^+(q,A^+(lambda,q))
+b p_s^-(q,A^-(lambda,q)),

and after the global q equation is solved,
P=P(lambda).

This is the intended reduced UCFT architecture: the two local steel amplitudes are algebraically condensed, leaving only the global equilibrium variable q outside the UHPC material evaluation.

## E. Post-yield boundary

The elastic strain relation above is exact only before the generalized plate enters its reduced plastic branch.

The previously proposed edge-yield consistency envelope p_s^Y(q,A) gives a descending force-amplitude relation, but by itself it does NOT supply the post-yield end-shortening law A(lambda,q). Under ideal plasticity, plastic shortening is not determined from stress alone.

Therefore one must not silently continue
lambda_s=p_s/(E_s t_s)+gbar_s
with p_s=p_s^Y after first yield.

A true S2 descending displacement-controlled path requires one generalized plastic evolution/work relation. Chen Ji Fig.8.19 itself states that the post-edge-yield ultimate path normally requires numerical treatment; Yun Lu stops at first edge yield. Until a reduced plastic evolution law is derived, p_s^Y is a load-amplitude envelope, not a complete lambda-path law.

## F. UHPC physical-anchor framework

A universal UHPC global law should be generated from a small set of physical descriptors rather than UC141-specific rows.

Compression anchors:
1. sigma(0)=0, sigma'(0)=E_c.
2. Near-linear anchor: at sigma_c=0.8 f_c use epsilon_c,80=0.8 f_c/E_c. FHWA reports UHPC compression is close to linear to about 80–90% of peak.
3. Compression peak: (-epsilon_cp,-f_c), with zero tangent.
4. Post-peak half-strength:
(-kappa_c50 epsilon_cp,-0.5 f_c).

For the common descending reference
y=x/[beta_c(x-1)^2+x],
the half-strength strain ratio is

kappa_c50 =
[2beta_c+1+sqrt(4beta_c+1)]/(2beta_c),

or equivalently
beta_c=kappa_c50/(kappa_c50-1)^2.

The common Yang-type beta_c=2 gives kappa_c50=2 exactly.
Other published complete-curve models use larger descending parameters, so kappa_c50 must remain a material descriptor rather than being universally fixed.

Tension anchors:
1. common origin slope E_c;
2. tensile peak (epsilon_tp,f_t), zero tangent;
3. localization point (epsilon_tloc,f_tloc);
4. tensile limit epsilon_tlim.

Hiew 2024 directly supports the need for distinct cracking/peak/localization/limit descriptors. In the reported fibre-reinforced series the localization stress is typically only modestly below the tensile peak while the tensile limit is commonly about 0.8–1.2%.

Recommended physical domain:
[-5 epsilon_cp, epsilon_tlim].

The compression bound -5epsilon_cp is a computational/material-curve range, not a statement that stress vanishes there. For the common beta_c=2 descending law, the residual compression at 5epsilon_cp is 5/37=0.1351 f_c.

The tensile side should not use +5epsilon_tp universally: for long strain-hardening UHPC this can extend far beyond localization/pull-out limits. epsilon_tlim is the more physical right boundary. If epsilon_tlim is unavailable, a declared engineering cap may be used, but it is not a universal material constant.

A candidate final formal family must remain ONE ordinary-epsilon expression. A suitable constrained rational-Hermite family is

sigma_U(epsilon)=
epsilon [E_c+c2 epsilon+c3 epsilon^2+...+cp epsilon^(p-1)]/
{1+[d1 epsilon+d2 epsilon^2+...+dr epsilon^r]^2},

with the physical-anchor equations above used to determine coefficients and with whole-domain constraints:
sigma<0 for epsilon<0,
sigma>0 for epsilon>0,
sigma'>0 from compression peak to tensile peak,
sigma'<0 on both post-peak tails,
denominator>0 identically.

Previous low-order tests show that enforcing only the two peak points is insufficient for long strain-hardening UHPC. The cracking/localization scale must enter the calibration. The next order audit should therefore be performed using the physical anchor set, not by adding arbitrary polynomial degree.
